findings.finding: LDC's 70%-held Tranzit-Food processing plant at Nyirbator (Hungary) burned on 10 June 2026. LDC says the H1 accounts will carry the impact with NO insurance compensation, and local press put the preliminary damage at 'several tens of billions of forint' (roughly EUR 50-100m+ gross). The size is first disclosed in this release, so H1 net income is likely to print below last year's EUR 136.9m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior one-off of this kind at LDC was found. Last November's in-line H1 with guidance confirmed fell 4.4% ('LDC recule malgre une croissance semestrielle'), so this name sells headlines that disappoint.
findings.original_quote: les incidences de ce sinistre sur les comptes seront presentees lors de la publication des resultats semestriels [...] « a ce stade aucune compensation ne sera integree dans la cloture des comptes du 1er semestre 2026 » (the effects of the loss on the accounts will be presented with the half-year results [...] 'at this stage no compensation will be included in the H1 2026 closing'). Hungarian: 'elozetes becslesek szerint a kar tobb tizmilliard forint is lehet' (preliminary estimates: the damage could be several tens of billions of forint), vg.hu 2026-06-10
findings.why_not_priced: The fire and the no-compensation policy are public, but the amount is not, and the stock has drifted (-4.6% over 60 days, -3% on the revenue day) rather than gapped. Had a large charge been priced, the revenue-day fall would have been read as fire-driven. The press instead blamed a 'semestre convaincant qui ne seduit pas'. Insurance should recover most of it later, which the market may look through; hence the small size.
findings.independence: https://www.vg.hu/vilaggazdasag-magyar-gazdasag/2026/06/ipar-katasztrofa-tuz-nyirbator (2026-06-10, damage estimate, 500 employees, finished-goods warehouse, production hall and inventory burned). Tranzit 70% stake: https://ca.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/LDC-31531420/news/L-D-C-S-A-agreed-to-acquire-70-stake-in-Tranzit-Ker-Kereskedelmi-Zartkoruen-Mukodo-Reszvenytarsas-34694505

findings.finding: Two brokers (TP ICAP Midcap, target EUR 141; Portzamparc) called the > EUR 7.7bn revenue guide 'particulierement prudent': it needs only +3.3% H2 growth, which Green Label's full-period consolidation could deliver alone. That leaves room for a revenue-guide raise in a release that will at least confirm the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: April 2026: Q4 revenue with an upward revision of objectives; May 2026: FY beat (ROC about 12% above consensus per EuroLand) and new 2030 plan, +5.7% the next day. November 2025 H1: guide only confirmed, -4.4%. October 2026 H1 revenue: guide confirmed, -3% intraday.
findings.original_quote: Portzamparc juge particulierement prudent l'objectif annuel de chiffre d'affaires de 7,7 milliards d'euros, qui implique une croissance de seulement 3,3% au second semestre (Portzamparc considers the EUR 7.7bn annual revenue target particularly cautious, implying only 3.3% H2 growth)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it is in the wire copy. But the stock fell 3% that day and sits about 27% below TP ICAP's EUR 141 target, so the market is not paying for a raise. If it were, the stock would have held up on the revenue print instead of drifting lower into the results. Kept small because LDC's habit is to confirm at H1 and raise in April.
findings.independence: Company arithmetic: H1 EUR 3,739.8m against H2 2025-26 of about EUR 3,833m (FY EUR 7,283.2m less H1 EUR 3,450m) already puts the FY above EUR 7.7bn at flat H2, https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/ldc-depasse-ses-objectifs-annuels-et-vise-10-milliards-deuros-de-chiffre-daffa_697431

findings.finding: International (FY margin 7.2% on exceptional 2025 prices) entered price deflation. The company reported Q2 LFL sales +0.1% with Polish/Hungarian daily-chicken prices -12%. The EU series shows output +5.1% in Jan-Apr 2026 (Hungary +21.7%, Poland +15.1%) and broiler prices below 2025, which argues for a lower H1 International margin and cautious H2 wording. Lower feed costs (FAS Warsaw) partly cushion it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No segment-level reaction history was found. International's rise from 4.2% to 7.2% margin drove last year's FY beat and the +5.7% reaction.
findings.original_quote: LDC evoque un ralentissement de la dynamique de vente, qu'il explique « principalement par les tensions sur les prix du poulet du quotidien en baisse de 12% (Pologne / Hongrie) » apres des niveaux « exceptionnellement eleves en 2025 » (LDC cites a sales slowdown 'mainly due to everyday-chicken prices down 12% (Poland/Hungary)' after 'exceptionally high 2025' levels)
findings.why_not_priced: The sales effect is public, but the margin effect is not: International is about 19% of sales and carried the highest divisional margin, and nobody has published what -12% pricing does to it. Net of the rest of the company: Volaille France (+4% price/mix) and Traiteur (+18%, Pierre Martinet) can offset, and feed-cost relief cushions it, so the size is small.
findings.independence: https://zootecnicainternational.com/?p=18746 (2026-08-18, EC dashboard: EU output +5.1%, prices below 2025). Counter-evidence, which sets the size: https://www.thepoultrysite.com/news/2026/09/polands-chicken-production-set-to-rise-3-7-in-2027 (feed costs declined through H1 2026)

findings.finding: France raised its highly pathogenic avian influenza risk level to the maximum from Friday 20 November 2026, the week of the print. The H2 outlook (Christmas season, turkey still recovering from the late-FY2025-26 outbreak) will likely carry vigilance language.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last season's raise came on 22 Oct 2025 and was followed by 156 outbreaks; LDC still confirmed at H1 (stock -4.4%) and raised in April.
findings.original_quote: Grippe aviaire en France : le niveau de risque releve au maximum des vendredi (avian flu in France: risk level raised to maximum from Friday)
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company and public: this is a hypothesis about the outlook wording, not a company number, so it is small. The stock's -2.8% five-day drift fits it being partly in already.
findings.independence: LDC's own 7 Oct release ties the Volaille volume decline to turkey recovering 'apres un episode d'influenza aviaire survenu en fin d'exercice 2025-2026': https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/ldc-affiche-3-74-milliards-deuros-de-chiffre-daffaires-au-1er-semestre-et-conf_703848

baseline_tension: There is no real lean to beat (+0.04, run-up-driven, truncated-zero short register). The small negative sum agrees with the mild 5- and 60-day drift rather than cutting against it, so part of it is plausibly priced.
language_note: The French press (ABC Bourse, EasyBourse/Zonebourse, Boursorama/EuroLand) carried the company's own wording that the fire will be quantified at H1 with no insurance compensation; no English source reached in this hunt carried it
The Hungarian local press (vg.hu), not French or English, carried the only damage estimate ('several tens of billions of forint')

The broker views (TP ICAP EUR 141 target, Portzamparc 'particulierement prudent') and last year's 'conformes aux attentes' H1 came only from French wires; English searches returned Louis Dreyfus Company noise
The issuer's French agenda page plus the AMF flux timestamps settled the session (amc); no English source gave a time
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the pre-released revenue-mix finding moved from +0.2 to 0.0
'A beat made of a one-off is sold' / one-off at a fraction of operating money: the fire charge moved from -0.8 to -0.6, since it sits below ROC and insurance should recover most of it later

'Size the move on what is new; let reaction history move p_up, not abs_move_pct': abs_move_pct went from 4.5 to 5.0, because H1 profit lines and the fire are unseen numbers and France's median print move is 4.19%; p_up stays at 46
Positioning: the zero is explicitly a truncation floor with anchor_covered false, not 'nobody is short'
Session: session_check opens with 'amc' and cites the timestamps, which the resolver reads
